Peon

PEE-on · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Peon is a person of low rank who performs menial or unskilled labor, especially one with little power or status.

After ten years at the company, she still felt like a peon, stuck doing the same photocopying tasks as her first week.

Worked Example

The new hire quickly realized that despite his fancy diploma, he was treated as just another peon in the mailroom.

Calling someone a peon usually points out that they have little power or status in an organization, even if the word is sometimes used half-jokingly.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

laborer: a person who does hard physical work, often for low pay

underling: a person in a subordinate or low-ranking position

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

potentate: a ruler who holds great power

aristocrat: a member of the highest social class, often by birth

Where it sits · how little status and freedom remain — worker → peon → serf

worker vs. peon: Worker is a neutral, respectful word for anyone who does a job, with no implication of low status.

serf vs. peon: A serf goes further still -- a laborer legally bound to work land they don't own, with almost no personal freedom.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — peon

Root — peon: a foot soldier or day laborer (from Spanish peón, ultimately from Latin pes, pedis, 'foot')

Put it together

Put it together: Peon was borrowed whole from Spanish peón, 'a foot soldier' -- someone who fought or worked on foot rather than commanding from above -- which came to mean a low-ranking laborer. It traces ultimately back to Latin pes ('foot'), the same root behind pedestrian, but no piece of that Latin root is visible in the English spelling.

Use the root in a new word: pedestrian

Use the root in a new word: pedestrian: A pedestrian -- someone traveling on foot -- shares peon's same Latin root for 'foot.'

Peon can be used seriously to describe real economic exploitation, or more casually and half-jokingly to complain about being low on the totem pole at work or school.
